content:
Channing Tatum wants to make it clear that he is not behind a dedicated Instagram account mocking his ex-fiancée Zoë Kravitz.

On Monday, the "Avengers: Doomsday" actor denied rumors that he used a "finsta" account @bidness_nonya to mock Kravitz and her new fiancé Harry Styles. Fans began suspecting him over the weekend after connecting the dots.

The rumor gained momentum because internet users noticed Tatum appeared to be the account's only follower, and the account has since been deactivated or deleted.

The account had previously left mean-spirited comments under Kravitz and Styles's posts, including one under a related post that read: "Spreading hate on purpose."

In an Instagram Story, Tatum wrote: "Yo I can't believe people think I have nothing better to do than be on this app all day glazing myself, this is wild." He also wrote: "Also if I was going to make a finsta, like really, would I follow myself? You guys really think I'm that stupid?"

He added: "Wake up, guys. But if you guys really need me to spell it out for you, I only have one IG and it's @channingtatum."

The mystery account's actual holder had directly told an internet follower that "I am not (Tatum)," Cosmopolitan reported.

HuffPost has reached out to Tatum, Kravitz, and Styles for comment.

Tatum and Kravitz were first linked in August 2021 while working on Kravitz's directorial debut, "Blink Twice." They got engaged in 2023 but called off their wedding plans in October 2024.

People confirmed Styles and Kravitz got engaged after eight months of dating, with the news announced in April. Kravitz had previously been spotted wearing a large diamond ring on her left ring finger and kissing her boyfriend in London. A source told the outlet that the couple shared the news with only a small circle of close friends and family.

There are reports Tatum is now dating Australian model Inka Williams.
